etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English either, from Old English ǣġhwæþer, from *aiwon + *gahwaþera. Akin to Old Saxon eogihwethar, iahwethar (Low German jeed); Old Dutch *iogewether, *iowether, *iother (Dutch ieder); Old High German eogihwedar, iegihweder, ieweder (German jeder).

definitions.definition: (often proscribed) Any one (of more than two).

definitions.definition: One or the other of two people or things.

definitions.definition: Introduces the first of two (or occasionally more) options or possibilities, the second (or last) of which is introduced by “or”.
